LESSON: READING FOR FLUENCY, SCANNING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Reading 2.2 Speed Reading (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, the learner
Topic 2.4: Reading for fluency, Scanning for information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading for fluency, Scanning for information. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you improve your reading fluency?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify specific information for comprehension
2. read given texts fluently for communication
3. appreciate the role of correct pronunciation in reading comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING FOR FLUENCY, SCANNING FOR INFORMATION
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading for fluency, Scanning for information helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING FOR FLUENCY, SCANNING FOR INFORMATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify specific information for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify specific information for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify specific information for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading for fluency, Scanning for information”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify specific information for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read given texts fluently for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to read given texts fluently for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read given texts fluently for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading for fluency, Scanning for information to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read given texts fluently for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of correct pronunciation in reading comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of correct pronunciation in reading comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of correct pronunciation in reading comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of correct pronunciation in reading comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading for fluency, Scanning for information is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading for fluency, Scanning for information”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify specific information for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading for fluency, Scanning for information to a partner. (skill: read given texts fluently for communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of correct pronunciation in reading comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading for fluency, Scanning for information to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify specific information for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: read given texts fluently for communication.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of correct pronunciation in reading comprehension.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading for fluency, Scanning for information from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading for fluency, Scanning for information: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading for fluency, Scanning for information?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you improve your reading fluency?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading for fluency, Scanning for information means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify specific information for comprehension.
5. Be able to: read given texts fluently for communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
